blogs.title: The Pulmonary Mask: When the Pancreas Hides Behind the Pleura
blogs.description: This post explores the anatomical mechanism by which pancreatic fluid tracks retroperitoneally through the esophageal or aortic hiatus to create a pleural effusion, and how this leads to the classic diagnostic trap of PPF: respiratory symptoms with an abdominal source. We discuss why over 68% of PPF cases present with predominant thoracic complaints and fewer than 20% with abdominal symptoms, review the natural diaphragmatic pathways of pancreatic leakage, and offer a framework for when to suspect a pancreatic etiology in any patient with recurrent, unilateral, hemorrhagic pleural effusion of unclear origin.

blogs.title: Pleural Fluid Amylase: The Most Underutilized Test in Unexplained Effusions
blogs.description: A deep dive into pleural fluid amylase and lipase as diagnostic tools. We cover when to send them, the pathognomonic threshold (amylase ≥1000 IU/L), and the critical role of amylase isoenzyme typing to distinguish pancreatic-type from salivary-type amylase. We review the differential of amylase-rich pleural effusions—including Boerhaave syndrome, malignancy, and tuberculosis—and provide a practical algorithm for incorporating pleural fluid amylase into the routine workup of recurrent or atypical pleural effusions.

blogs.title: Anchoring Bias in Action: From Empiric TB Therapy to Pancreatopleural Fistula
blogs.description: A cognitive autopsy of this case exploring how anchoring bias and premature closure led to empiric antitubercular therapy based on a mildly elevated pleural fluid ADA and a positive Koch's contact history, while the true diagnosis remained hidden. We examine the diagnostic errors at each of the three admissions, discuss how the repeat thoracentesis of dark red fluid should have triggered a broader differential earlier, and offer practical debiasing strategies—such as forced consideration of non-pulmonary causes and the value of repeated history-taking—to avoid similar pitfalls.

blogs.title: From CT to MRCP to ERCP: Imaging the Invisible Leak
blogs.description: An imaging-focused review comparing the roles of contrast-enhanced CT, MRCP, and ERCP in diagnosing PPF. We discuss why CT, while useful for identifying pseudocysts and calcifications, visualizes the actual fistula in only 33–47% of cases, while MRCP offers 70–80% sensitivity for fistula and duct anatomy. We also review when to escalate to ERCP—the gold standard for therapeutic planning—and provide a stepwise imaging algorithm for suspected PPF in both pediatric and adult populations.

blogs.title: Conservative vs. Invasive: Navigating the Management of Pancreatopleural Fistula
blogs.description: This post breaks down the treatment ladder for PPF, from conservative measures (bowel rest, TPN, octreotide, PERT, thoracic drainage) to endoscopic intervention (transpapillary stenting) and surgery (distal pancreatectomy, Puestow procedure). We highlight the sobering 12% success rate of conservative management in pediatric cases versus the near-100% acute success of ERCP and 93% success of surgery, discuss the optimal duration of conservative therapy before escalation, and address the lack of standardized guidelines for this rare condition.

blogs.title: Pediatric PPF: Why Children Are a Different Animal Than Adults
blogs.description: An exploration of the unique etiologic, genetic, and clinical features of PPF in children compared to adults. We contrast the predominance of chronic alcoholic pancreatitis in adults (up to 99% in some series) with the role of genetic mutations (PRSS1, SPINK1, CFTR, CTRC) and blunt abdominal trauma in children. We discuss when to pursue genetic testing in pediatric pancreatitis, the importance of detailed family history, and why pediatric PPF may be under-recognized due to its rarity and atypical presentations.
